outcomes.text: Explain the principles behind AI operation.
Choose suitable AI tools for different tasks.
Use current AI tools competently and adapt to new developments.
Explain AI’s advantages and disadvantages for society.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.description: Introduces data-science reasoning, statistical and computational ideas, ethical practice and communicating results.

courses.name: AI Unlocked for Curious Minds
courses.description: Introduces AI concepts, practical uses, limitations and social implications for students across disciplines.

courses.name: Ethics of AI and Societal Decision Making
courses.description: Applies ethical reasoning to data-intensive systems, including fairness, transparency and accountability.

courses.name: AI-Powered Exploration and Discovery
courses.description: Uses accessible AI tools for research, writing, analysis, media and coding, with practical prompt design.

courses.name: Human-Centered AI
courses.description: Examines reliable and accountable AI design that supports human needs and reduces harms.

courses.name: Lessons Learned from Failures of Data-Driven Systems in Society
courses.description: Uses interdisciplinary research to examine failures and social consequences of data-driven systems; no technical background is required.

courses.name: Research-Methods for Socially Responsible AI: An Ethical Expedition
courses.description: Team research examines socially responsible AI through a semester project with faculty and graduate teaching support.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisite, DATA 120 or permission from the instructor.

requirements.title: Minor total
requirements.summary: Complete the published 15 semester-hour minor. The elective pool is not an additional requirement.

requirements.title: Required core
requirements.summary: Complete all three core courses.

requirements.title: Minor electives
requirements.summary: Choose 2 courses totaling 6 semester hours from the published pool.

requirements.title: Minor residence
requirements.summary: Complete at least nine core semester hours at UNC–Chapel Hill.

requirements.title: Minor GPA
requirements.summary: Earn at least 2.000 cumulative GPA in minor core coursework.

requirements.title: Honors alternatives
requirements.summary: An honors version meets the same requirement; applicable honors enrollment and GPA restrictions still apply. DATA 110 and DATA 120 are marked as offering honors versions.

requirements.title: Minor combinations
requirements.summary: At most two minors are allowed. Academic units may exclude particular major/minor combinations. A College of Arts and Sciences student needs the professional school’s permission for a minor there.

requirements.title: Exclusive minor work
requirements.summary: More than half of both core courses and credit hours, including cross-listed work, must be exclusive to this minor versus other majors/minors. Units may further restrict general-education overlap.

requirements.title: Exam credit limit
requirements.summary: At most one course of 3–4 BE credit hours can count toward a minor.

requirements.title: Pass/fail in a minor
requirements.summary: Gateway, prerequisite and additional-requirement courses cannot be elected pass/fail. One PS course, but not LP, may meet minor core requirements.

requirements.title: Declaration timing
requirements.summary: Declaring by early junior year is encouraged, not presented as a mandatory admission deadline.

requirements.title: Cross-school permissions
requirements.summary: Professional-school students need their school and the relevant receiving school’s permission for an outside minor; a College of Arts and Sciences minor requires that college’s permission too.

requirements.title: Concurrent subjects and overlap counting
requirements.summary: College of Arts and Sciences students may study at most three subjects in the listed major/minor combinations. Same-unit combinations are subject to departmental restrictions and the 45-hour subject limit. A lecture/lab combination counts as one course for overlap.

requirements.title: Credit unit
requirements.summary: UNC values degree credit in semester hours; the catalog defines classroom, independent work and laboratory/studio expectations.

requirements.title: Transfer approval
requirements.summary: Transfer credit requires an official final transcript; supporting course documentation may be required. Current students need term-specific advance course approval, and graduation clearance deadlines apply.

requirements.title: External grades and credit
requirements.summary: External courses require C or higher. External grades do not enter UNC cumulative GPA. UNC converts other credit scales into semester hours; zero-credit courses do not transfer.

requirements.title: Transfer ceiling
requirements.summary: Once the 75-hour transfer maximum is reached, no additional credit or substitutions are posted; this university ceiling does not replace the minor’s nine-hour UNC residence rule.

requirements.title: Transfer equivalence and age
requirements.summary: Equivalence normally uses 70% content alignment, subject to accreditation, sequence, rigor and discipline exceptions. Upper-division courses and courses at least ten years old require department review. Approved study abroad is handled by the designated global offices; international transcripts require a course-by-course WES evaluation.

requirements.title: Departmental examination credit
requirements.summary: Department and school/college approval is required at least 30 days before an exam. The exam must precede the final semester or full summer session before graduation.

requirements.title: Repeated courses
requirements.summary: A nonrepeatable course earns degree credit only once, using the highest passing grade (later attempt if tied); all attempt grades remain in cumulative GPA.

requirements.title: PS/LP grading
requirements.summary: PS corresponds to A–C; LP corresponds to C−, D+ or D. PS/LP do not affect GPA; F does. One PS core course may count, and students cannot change a major/minor merely to elect pass/fail. Elections are final.

requirements.title: Pass/fail declaration window
requirements.summary: Submit the ConnectCarolina form from the fifth class day through the end of week eight; consulting an advisor is recommended.

requirements.title: Pass/fail university limits
requirements.summary: At most one student-elected course per semester; 23 total pass/fail hours, with at most 16 elected and 13 established hours. Summer, honors and interinstitutional courses, general-education requirements, previously passed letter-graded courses and declared gateway/prerequisite/additional requirements cannot be elected pass/fail.

requirements.title: Exam and placement distinctions
requirements.summary: BE can award credit but does not meet minor GPA requirements; PL placement alone awards no credit hours.

notes: Completeness applies to the local minor inventory and applicable minor eligibility, overlap, residence, grade, transfer, examination and repeat policies; it does not certify the entire host bachelor’s degree.
All seven listed courses award three semester hours. The elective pool contains four alternatives, of which two are required; do not total the pool as compulsory coursework.

No prerequisites are stated in the reviewed DATA 110, DATA 117 and DATA 120 blocks; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment. DATA 520 explicitly permits instructor permission instead of DATA 120.
The catalog marks honors alternatives for DATA 110 and DATA 120; the standard versions form a complete route. Optional honors enrollment/GPA restrictions remain applicable.
Descriptions and learning outcomes are concise reviewed paraphrases. Course-credit units are verified from the linked Hours of Credit policy. No public course sites or example syllabi were reviewed.

First-offered date remains unknown. Official June 3, 2026 curriculum news lists the recently approved minor, and September 1, 2026 university news describes active students, but neither explicitly names the first-offered semester. School founding in 2026 is separate evidence.
